overview: Verisign operates the authoritative registry for the .com and .net generic top-level domains (gTLDs) under long-term agreements with ICANN and a Cooperative Agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce, providing the critical infrastructure that resolves domain names to IP addresses for the global internet. The company is effectively a regulated, royalty-like toll-booth business: it earns a fixed per-domain registry fee on every .com/.net registration and renewal, processed through a wholesale channel of accredited registrars (e.g., GoDaddy, Namecheap) rather than selling directly to end users. Substantially all revenue and profit come from the U.S. (.com/.net registry), though the names themselves are registered by individuals and businesses worldwide.

business_model.summary: Verisign is a wholesale registry operator, not a retail registrar. It charges ICANN-accredited registrars an annual per-domain fee (currently $10.26, rising to $10.97 on Nov 1, 2026) for every new .com registration and renewal; .net pricing is separately capped. Because renewals recur annually and the .com/.net domain base is massive (179.1 million names as of mid-2026), the revenue stream is highly recurring, predictable, and extremely high-margin (operating margins near 68-70%) with minimal incremental cost to serve additional names.

revenue_streams.name: Other TLDs / registry services (.gov, .jobs, .name, new gTLD back-end services, security/naming services)

business_model.customer_type: B2B wholesale - ICANN-accredited registrars (GoDaddy, Namecheap, Tucows/OpenSRS, etc.) are the direct customers; end registrants are businesses and consumers worldwide
business_model.geographic_mix: Revenue is almost entirely contracted and billed in the U.S. (registry fees paid by U.S. and internationally based registrars), though underlying domain registrants are global; no meaningful foreign-currency revenue exposure

main_competitors: New alternative gTLDs and social/search platforms as de facto domain substitutes
competitive_position.market_position: Sole, exclusive operator of .com and .net under contract - a legal and structural monopoly in the two largest gTLDs, which together still represent roughly half of all registered domain names globally

moat_factors.description: Sole-source Cooperative Agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce and Registry Agreements with ICANN give Verisign exclusive, long-dated rights to operate .com (through 2030 with presumptive renewal) and .net; no competitive bidding for these TLDs has occurred in over two decades
29+ consecutive years of 100% uptime for .com/.net resolution; switching the world's default TLD infrastructure would be operationally and politically disruptive
.com is the default, most-trusted and most-recognized TLD; new registrants overwhelmingly default to .com over alternatives, reinforcing demand even as new TLDs proliferate

Amendment 35 to the Cooperative Agreement (2018) permits up to 7% annual .com wholesale price increases in 4 of every 6 years, giving Verisign a quasi-guaranteed pricing tailwind independent of volume

moat_factors.factor: High operating leverage / low incremental cost
moat_factors.description: Fixed-cost infrastructure means each additional domain name registration carries near-zero marginal cost, driving industry-leading margins

weaknesses: Near-total revenue concentration in a single product (.com) that it does not control the pricing ceiling or contract renewal terms for - both set by the U.S. government/ICANN
No organic product diversification; new gTLD and security initiatives (.web, PKI/Zero Trust products) remain small relative to the core registry business
Negative stockholders' equity (-$2.25 billion) from aggressive buybacks funded partly by debt, increasing financial leverage
Structural exposure to secular share loss of .com/.net in favor of ccTLDs (.io, .ai, .co) and new gTLDs, particularly among tech/AI-native businesses

growth_drivers: Contracted wholesale price increases on .com (7% increases permitted in 4 of 6 years under Amendment 35; next hike $10.26 to $10.97 effective Nov 1, 2026) provide a predictable revenue tailwind independent of volume

AI-driven demand for new websites and digital presence is cited by management as accelerating domain registrations - record 12.7 million new registrations in Q2 2026 and raised full-year domain base growth guidance to 5.2%-6%
Large, aggressive share buyback program ($1.50 billion total authorization as of July 2026) mechanically shrinks share count and supports EPS growth even with modest top-line growth

New .web gTLD delegated into the root zone in 2026 with full wholesale pricing flexibility (unlike legacy .com/.net), opening a small but higher-margin incremental TLD opportunity ahead of expected general availability in late 2026/early 2027
New security/PKI ('Zero Trust') products aimed at AI-era authentication and digital-credibility needs, an embryonic diversification beyond pure registry fees
Participation under consideration in the 2026 ICANN new gTLD application round (window closed Aug 2026), which could add further TLDs to the portfolio with launches expected around 2028
International internet penetration growth and continued SMB/entrepreneurial formation support long-term unit growth in domain registrations

business.description: Management has flagged a 'challenge' expected in H2 2026 as a large cohort of late-2025 registrations reaches first-time renewal, where renewal rates (mid-40% range) run far below renewed-name rates (mid-80% range)

Alternative TLDs (.io, .ai, .co, and ICANN's expanding new gTLD program) and even search/social platforms acting as de facto navigation substitutes could erode .com's share of new registrations over time, especially among AI-native and tech-forward businesses
Virtually all revenue depends on two legacy TLDs; the company has limited ability to organically diversify given regulatory constraints on what it can offer

financial.risk: Negative stockholders' equity and rising debt
financial.description: Stockholders' deficit of roughly -$2.25 billion as of mid-2026, built via years of debt-funded buybacks; total debt around $2.3+ billion including notes due 2027/2031/2032, which raises refinancing and rate-sensitivity considerations even though cash flow comfortably covers interest
Nearly all free cash flow is returned via repurchases rather than dividends or diversifying M&A, leaving EPS growth reliant on continued buyback pace and share price levels

regulatory.risk: Loss or unfavorable renewal of .com Registry Agreement / Cooperative Agreement
regulatory.description: ICANN and the U.S. Department of Commerce could decline to renew, impose unfavorable terms, or restrict pricing flexibility at the next renewal/amendment cycle; the .com Registry Agreement was renewed through 2030 but any future unilateral amendment rights sought by ICANN remain a structural risk

Advocacy groups (e.g., American Economic Liberties Project) and some registrant/registrar commentary have publicly criticized Verisign's pricing flexibility as monopolistic; renewed Congressional or DOJ/DOC scrutiny could pressure future pricing terms
ICANN retains authority to adopt Consensus Policies that could impose new compliance costs or operating constraints on registry operations

macro.description: New domain registrations correlate with new business and website formation; a global economic slowdown could dampen new-registration growth, though renewals provide a stable base
Fixed-rate note structure limits near-term rate risk, but refinancing of 2027/2031/2032 maturities at higher rates than legacy issuance could modestly raise interest expense

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global domain name industry continues modest unit growth (low-to-mid single digits) with regulated pricing increases providing most of the revenue growth for legacy gTLD operators; AI-driven digital presence formation is cited as a 2025-2026 tailwind for new registrations
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - renewal-based recurring revenue model provides significant resilience; new registration volume has some sensitivity to small-business/entrepreneurial activity but overall demonstrated low cyclicality through past downturns
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-moderate - fixed-rate debt limits near-term impact, but elevated leverage (negative equity) increases sensitivity to refinancing conditions
key_input_costs: Data center / infrastructure operating costs (largely fixed)

recent_developments.event: Reported revenue of $435 million (+6% YoY), diluted EPS of $2.38, record 12.7 million new domain registrations in the quarter; domain base reached 179.1 million names
Raised and narrowed full-year 2026 domain name base growth guidance to 5.2%-6%; raised full-year revenue guidance to $1.745-$1.755 billion and operating income guidance to $1.185-$1.195 billion
Board increased share buyback authorization by $884.2 million, bringing total repurchase capacity to $1.50 billion with no expiration
Announced .com wholesale registry fee increase from $10.26 to $10.97 (up ~7%), effective November 1, 2026, under the pricing flexibility granted by Amendment 35 to the Cooperative Agreement

Successfully delegated the .web gTLD into the global DNS root zone with full wholesale pricing flexibility (unlike legacy .com/.net); general availability expected late 2026 or early 2027 following security testing and trademark sunrise periods

Management publicly attributed accelerating domain registration growth partly to AI tools lowering the friction of website/content creation and increasing demand for 'digital credibility,' alongside effective registrar marketing programs
Issued $550 million of 5.10% Senior Notes due 2031, using proceeds plus cash on hand to redeem the $550 million of 4.75% Senior Notes due 2027
Berkshire Hathaway trimmed its VeriSign stake by roughly 32%, selling 4.3 million shares while remaining one of the company's largest shareholders (~9.7% of shares outstanding after the sale)
Management guided to an expected renewal-rate headwind in the second half of 2026 due to a larger mix of first-time-renewing names from strong late-2025 registration cohorts

items.notes: Raised from prior full-year guidance following strong Q2 domain registration growth
Implies continued operating margin in the high-60s percent range
Up from an earlier FY2026 range closer to 3.1%-4.3% guided in Q1 2026; reflects record new-registration momentum partly attributed to AI-driven demand
Modest capex relative to revenue, consistent with the asset-light registry infrastructure model
No material change flagged from prior guidance
~7% increase under Amendment 35 pricing flexibility; part of a multi-year planned escalator

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jim Bidzos credited AI tools with making domain discovery, website creation, and content generation faster and easier, increasing the value of a distinct domain and 'digital credibility,' alongside effective registrar marketing, for driving 21% YoY growth in new unit registrations and a record quarterly registration count. Management flagged an expected renewal-rate headwind in H2 2026 tied to the mix shift toward first-time-renewing names from strong late-2025 cohorts, but otherwise described underlying demand trends as firm and reiterated confidence in raised full-year guidance.

bull_case: Durable, contract-protected monopoly on .com/.net registry operations with a built-in, government-sanctioned pricing escalator (up to 7% annually in 4 of every 6 years) that drives revenue growth largely independent of volume

Extremely high incremental margins (~68-70% operating margin) and minimal capex requirements generate substantial free cash flow, funding an aggressive buyback program ($1.50B authorization) that mechanically compounds EPS
AI-driven increase in website/business formation is providing an unexpected volume tailwind on top of the pricing escalator, with record new registrations and raised 2026 domain-base guidance
Long-term, high-profile holder (Berkshire Hathaway) lends credibility to the quality/moat thesis, and even its recent trim leaves it a top-15 Berkshire holding
Optionality from new initiatives (.web launch with full pricing flexibility, PKI/Zero Trust security products) offers modest incremental upside beyond the core legacy registry business
bear_case: Revenue is almost entirely dependent on a single contract (.com Registry Agreement/Cooperative Agreement) whose terms, renewal, and pricing flexibility are controlled by the U.S. government and ICANN, not Verisign - a renegotiation or unfavorable renewal is a structural tail risk

Negative stockholders' equity (-$2.25 billion) and growing debt load from years of debt-funded buybacks leave the balance sheet more levered than peers, raising refinancing risk as maturities approach
H2 2026 renewal-rate headwinds (large first-time-renewal cohort converting at much lower rates than seasoned names) could create a volume/revenue air pocket even amid strong new registrations

Long-term secular risk that alternative TLDs (ccTLDs like .io/.ai/.co), new gTLDs, and non-domain-based digital identity (social/app-based discovery) gradually erode .com's share of mind, particularly among newer AI-native businesses

Premium valuation (analyst targets clustering $270-$355) already prices in continued flawless execution of the pricing-escalator plus buyback algorithm, leaving limited margin for any growth or renewal-rate disappointment
